title: Published optical and infrared variability counts give weak adjusted constraints in 138 field dwarfs
abstract: We test the optical and infrared variability link in 180 published centred extreme-dust dwarfs. The raw odds ratio is 12.33. With W2 brightness, excess strength and kinematic group in a logistic model, it is 4.18 (95 percent profile interval 1.09-15.90). An exact test within brightness, excess and kinematic cells gives 3.77 (0.54-29.66; p = 0.220). Only 45 stars lie in cells with variable conditional counts. The 138 field-kinematics stars have seven infrared detections. Their adjusted odds ratio is 5.85 (0.71-36.55); their exact interval is 0.23 to infinity. Thus the pooled signal remains positive, but these data give weak evidence for a link within field stars after the tested adjustments. They do not show that a link is absent. Sparse cells, imperfect age labels, excess estimates and different survey epochs limit the inference. This is a new statistical analysis of fixed published measurements, with no new sky observations. We provide code, aggregate results, source hashes and numerical checks.

display.caption: Odds ratios for high optical scatter and infrared detection before and after adjustment. The field cell test has no finite upper limit.

citations.reason: Fixed sample, detections and derived statistics. We test the scope of the optical association after sensitivity adjustment.
Separate study of the kinematic detection contrast motivates explicit sensitivity adjustment.
